steps.text: This lsass.exe registry write alert involving a path with '\RunTime\' looks like it's probably a benign match against something like the Lsa RunTime key or Kerberos settings, so I want to check the actual relation to confirm.

arguments.reasoning: Read the registry write details (key path, value, process) to judge if it is an autostart entry.
Check the registry key path to see whether it is a real Run autostart key.
Verify lsass.exe image path, parent and signature.

steps.text: This registry value is a standard Windows secure time seeding entry written by lsass, so it's likely benign. I could check the accessing process further, but that's probably just sysmon or defender, so I'll mark this as benign.

submission.reasoning: The alert fired because the registry path contains the text '\Run', but it matched '\RunTime\', not a Run autostart key. lsass.exe, running from its normal location C:\windows\system32\lsass.exe on workstation5, set a QWORD value at HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\W32Time\SecureTimeLimits\RunTime\SecureTimeTickCount. Windows writes this value itself as part of Secure Time Seeding (Windows Time service), and the data is a tick count. It does not point to an executable, so it cannot start anything at logon. The rule simply matched part of a word. I found no sign of persistence or malicious behavior. I did not check the other process that accessed lsass, since the alert is only about the registry write.
